source_evidence.observation: For positive k, floating-point inputs a_1,...,a_{k-1}, b_1,...,b_k, c with b_k nonzero, and any evaluation order without underflow or overflow, the computed value satisfies an exact perturbed identity with coefficient bounds k*u; when b_k=1 and division is omitted, the bound is (k-1)*u.
For b_k=1, Theorem 3.1 gives |y_hat-y| <= (k-1)*u*(|y_hat| + sum |a_i*b_i|), from which the proof constructs sign-aligned coefficients using one real epsilon.
The nonzero general-divisor case is said to follow analogously from Corollary 3.2 with b=b_k, n=k, x_1=c, and x_{i+1}=-a_i*b_i.
The surrounding convention treats evaluation order as a rooted binary summation tree; c remains unperturbed, while superscripted perturbation coefficients may be pairwise distinct.
The paper uses finite floating-point numbers with radix beta and precision p, arbitrary round-to-nearest tie breaking, and unit roundoff u=(1/2)*beta^(1-p).
For real summands, each summand is first rounded and the rounded values are then added in an arbitrary order; choosing summands a_i*b_i gives the separate-product inner-product model used later.
The underlying theorem bounds a sum containing one exactly floating-point summand and other real summands whose initial roundings do not underflow.

source_evidence.anchor: Observations after Theorem 3.1 and first part of Corollary 3.2
source_evidence.observation: Overflow exclusion covers initial summand rounding and summation; Corollary 3.2 supplies the bound for a rounded division by a nonzero floating-point divisor.
For y_hat=fl(s_hat/b), the product b*y_hat used in the bound is exact mathematical multiplication, and the division contributes one u-sized error through equation (2.1b).
The improved coefficients are linear in u, contain no quadratic remainder, and impose no size restriction on the term count.

binders: Quantifier order: for every k in N_{>0}, every permitted tuple of scalar inputs, and every permitted summation order, if that execution avoids underflow and overflow, there exist real coefficients theta_k^(i), dependent on the inputs and execution, satisfying the identity and bounds. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement and proof]
The scalar inputs are a_1,...,a_{k-1}, b_1,...,b_{k-1}, b_k, c in F, with b_k != 0; no sign restriction is imposed on b_k. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
The nominal exact value is y=(c-sum_{i=1}^{k-1} a_i*b_i)/b_k, while y_hat denotes the result of its floating-point evaluation. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
The displayed coefficients are indexed by i=0 for the b_k*y_hat term and i=1,...,k-1 for the product terms. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity in Lemma 4.1]
hypotheses: k is any positive integer; the passage explicitly removes the former restriction on k. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Section 4.1 opening paragraph]
All named inputs belong to the finite floating-point set F and b_k is nonzero. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]

The expression is evaluated using the paper's separate floating-point product, binary summation, and final-division model, with arbitrary parenthesization of the summation. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), evaluation-order paragraph; PDF p. 6 (printed 689), paragraph following (2.4); PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1]

No underflow or overflow occurs in the relevant product roundings, summation, or final division. [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), observations after Theorem 3.1 and Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
conclusions: There exist real theta_k^(0),...,theta_k^(k-1) such that b_k*y_hat*(1+theta_k^(0)) = c - sum_{i=1}^{k-1} a_i*b_i*(1+theta_k^(i)), with |theta_k^(i)| <= k*u for every relevant i. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity in Lemma 4.1]

If b_k=1 and the division is omitted, the same identity has the sharper bounds |theta_k^(i)| <= (k-1)*u for every relevant i. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), sentence immediately following the displayed identity]
For b_k=1, the proof explicitly obtains |y_hat-y| <= (k-1)*u*(|y_hat|+sum_{i=1}^{k-1}|a_i*b_i|). [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 proof]

For b_k=1, the proof chooses epsilon in R with |epsilon| <= (k-1)*u and y_hat-y=epsilon*(|y_hat|+sum |a_i*b_i|), then sets epsilon^(0)=-sign(y_hat)*epsilon and epsilon^(i)=-sign(a_i*b_i)*epsilon for 1<=i<k to obtain the perturbed identity. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 proof]

The general b_k != 0 conclusion is obtained from Corollary 3.2, whose corresponding forward bound is |b_k*y_hat-(c-sum a_i*b_i)| <= k*u*(|b_k*y_hat|+sum |a_i*b_i|). [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), first bound of Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), final sentence of Lemma 4.1 proof]
definitions_and_conventions: F is a symmetric set of finite floating-point numbers containing zero, with radix beta>=2, precision p>=1, and a finite exponent range. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1 opening paragraphs]
fl is an arbitrary round-to-nearest map; ties may be resolved by any strategy. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), definition of fl]
The unit roundoff is u=(1/2)*beta^(1-p), hence u<=1/2. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), equations (2.1a)-(2.1b) and following paragraph]

The products a_i*b_i and b_k*y_hat appearing in the final identity are exact real products; rounding committed while computing products and division is absorbed into the coefficients. [PDF p. 6 (printed 689), paragraph following (2.4); PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 9 (printed 692), its proof]
The scalar c is intentionally unperturbed in the backward identity. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), paragraph following the evaluation-order examples]
Superscripts distinguish coefficients that may be pairwise different; the lemma does not assert one common coefficient for every term. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), footnote 1]
implicit_context: The result inherits the paper-wide round-to-nearest model for any radix, precision, and tie-breaking strategy. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 4 (printed 687), discussion following (1.8)]
The statement is scalar: k counts c together with k-1 signed product terms, not a matrix dimension. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), equations (1.3a) and (1.5b); PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1]

The existential coefficients may depend on the selected evaluation tree and on the computed result; they are not chosen uniformly before the computation. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), evaluation-order paragraph; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), constructive proof]

For b_k != 1, an analogous common-epsilon sign construction can be inferred by replacing y_hat in the unit-case construction with the exact quantity b_k*y_hat, but that formula is not written explicitly. [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), final sentence of Lemma 4.1 proof]

Although division by other values might happen to be exact, the sharper (k-1)*u conclusion is stated only for the algorithm variant b_k=1 with no division. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), sentence following the displayed Lemma 4.1 identity]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Compute each product a_i*b_i with its own floating-point rounding, combine c and the signed products -a_i*b_i using any rooted binary summation tree, and, when b_k != 1, round the final division of the computed numerator by b_k; when b_k=1 the division is omitted. The formal order freedom concerns the binary summation tree and does not describe fused multiply-add or reassociation of the final division. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), evaluation-order paragraph; PDF p. 6 (printed 689), paragraph following (2.4); PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1]
numerical_model: Arithmetic uses finite floating-point numbers and rounding to nearest, with arbitrary tie breaking. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1]
When neither underflow nor overflow occurs, fl(t)=t*(1+delta_1)=t/(1+delta_2), with |delta_1|,|delta_2|<=u. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), equations (2.1a)-(2.1b)]

For the division, y_hat=fl(s_hat/b_k), and b_k*y_hat in the analysis is an exact real product rather than an additional rounded operation. [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), first part of Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 9 (printed 692), first paragraph of its proof]

The inner-product model separately rounds each exact product a_i*b_i before binary summation; no fused operation is part of the stated model. [PDF p. 6 (printed 689), equation (2.4) and following paragraph]
error_notions: The principal result is a componentwise backward representation: c is exact, while the output-side term and each exact product receive separate multiplicative perturbations. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), equation (1.5b) and following discussion; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 identity]
Coefficient size is measured by scalar absolute value, uniformly bounded by k*u or, in the no-division case, (k-1)*u. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]

The unit-divisor proof first establishes an absolute forward residual bound weighted by |y_hat| and the sum of absolute exact products, then converts it to the backward identity by sign alignment. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 proof]
The displayed backward identity is an exact real equality; it is not an equality only up to neglected rounding terms. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity and proof]
norms: Only scalar absolute values occur in Lemma 4.1 and its proof; no vector or matrix norm is part of this result. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement and proof]

The forward residual uses the componentwise weight |y_hat|+sum |a_i*b_i|, or |b_k*y_hat|+sum |a_i*b_i| in the general-divisor case. [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 proof]
constants_and_indexing: There are k signed summands in the numerator: c and k-1 products indexed i=1,...,k-1. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), equation (1.3a); PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1]
The perturbation index i=0 belongs to b_k*y_hat, while indices 1,...,k-1 belong to the corresponding product terms. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity]
The general constant is exactly k*u; the no-division constant is exactly (k-1)*u, while the theta subscript remains k in both displays. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
k=1 is not excluded by k in N_{>0}; under the standard empty-sum convention the unit-divisor bound becomes zero. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 binder and displayed ranges]
No hypothesis k*u<1 or (k-1)*u<1 is imposed. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Section 4.1 opening paragraph]
higher_order_terms: The bounds k*u and (k-1)*u contain no gamma denominator and no stated O(u^2) remainder. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Section 4.1 opening paragraph and Lemma 4.1]
No terms are omitted from the exact perturbed identity. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity and proof]

The absence of a term-count restriction remains valid even when k*u>=1; the paper does not require the factors 1+theta_k^(i) to be positive or nonzero. [PDF p. 4 (printed 687), discussion following (1.8); PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Section 4.1 opening paragraph]
exceptional_values: b_k must be nonzero, excluding division by zero; it need not be positive. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
The inputs are finite floating-point values; infinities are not members of F. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1 definition of F]
Underflow is defined as an inexact rounding of a real value in the subnormal range; an exact subnormal result is therefore allowed. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1 underflow definition]

Under the paper's convention floating-point addition cannot underflow, whereas multiplication and division can; Lemma 4.1 nevertheless states the blanket absence of both underflow and overflow. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), end of Section 2.1; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
Zero values of c, a_i, b_i, products, and y_hat are not excluded; only b_k is required to be nonzero. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), F contains zero; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 binders]

undebatable_constraints: The contract must quantify over every positive k, every listed floating-point input tuple with b_k nonzero, and every permitted summation tree, followed by existential perturbation coefficients. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement; PDF p. 3 (printed 686), evaluation-order paragraph]

The exact identity must be b_k*y_hat*(1+theta_k^(0)) = c - sum_{i=1}^{k-1} a_i*b_i*(1+theta_k^(i)); c cannot be perturbed or omitted. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity; PDF p. 3 (printed 686), paragraph after (1.5)]
Every relevant coefficient has the general bound |theta_k^(i)|<=k*u. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
The sharper |theta_k^(i)|<=(k-1)*u bound is claimed specifically when b_k=1 and division is omitted. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), sentence following the displayed identity]
The result assumes round-to-nearest arithmetic and excludes underflow and overflow. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]

The result permits arbitrary binary summation order but uses separately rounded products and a final rounded division rather than an FMA model. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), evaluation-order paragraph; PDF p. 6 (printed 689), paragraph after (2.4); PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2]

The factors b_k*y_hat and a_i*b_i in the final identity are exact mathematical products, not newly rounded quantities. [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 9 (printed 692), its proof; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1]
No k*u<1 condition, gamma factor, or higher-order remainder may be added. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Section 4.1 opening paragraph]

The unit-case proof's sign-aligned construction must be preserved as a particular witness construction, without strengthening the lemma to require all admissible coefficient families to share one magnitude. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), footnote 1; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 proof]

ambiguities.issue: The proof uses sign(y_hat) and sign(a_i*b_i) but does not define sign at zero in the selected passage or the preceding floating-point definitions. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Sections 2.1-2.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 proof]
ambiguities.evidence: Zero inputs and a zero computed result are allowed, yet the proof states |epsilon^(i)|=|epsilon| after multiplying epsilon by sign of the corresponding quantity. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), unit-case construction]
ambiguities.impact: With the conventional sign(0)=0, the claimed equality of magnitudes fails for a zero term, although the perturbed identity and required upper bounds remain obtainable; a formalization must specify a nonzero sign choice at zero or weaken that intermediate equality. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), unit-case construction]

ambiguities.issue: The explicit sign formulas are written only for b_k=1; the general-divisor proof is summarized as analogous. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), final paragraph of Lemma 4.1 proof]
ambiguities.evidence: Corollary 3.2 supplies a residual weighted by |b_k*y_hat|, but Lemma 4.1 does not explicitly write the corresponding general-case epsilon or signs. [PDF p. 8 (printed 691), first Corollary 3.2 bound; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), proof ending]
ambiguities.impact: Using theta_k^(0)=-sign(b_k*y_hat)*epsilon in the general case is a justified inference, not an explicitly displayed source formula; the authoritative claim is existence of bounded coefficients.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'whatever the order of evaluation' could be read broadly in isolation. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 statement]
ambiguities.evidence: The paper formally explains it through rooted binary trees for the summation, with products as leaves and the division treated separately. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), paragraph following (1.5c); PDF p. 8 (printed 691), Corollary 3.2]
ambiguities.impact: The claim should not be silently extended to fused multiply-add evaluation, movement of the division inside the summation, or arbitrary algebraic rewrites.

ambiguities.issue: The phrase 'for all i' does not separately spell out its index set. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed Lemma 4.1 identity]
ambiguities.evidence: The display contains theta_k^(0) on the left and theta_k^(i) under a sum indexed i=1,...,k-1 on the right. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), displayed identity]
ambiguities.impact: The natural contract range is i=0,...,k-1; a formal target should not introduce a coefficient at i=k or omit the output-side coefficient i=0.

contract_plain_english: For any positive k and finite floating-point scalars a_1,...,a_{k-1}, b_1,...,b_k, c with b_k nonzero, compute the products separately, sum c-sum a_i*b_i using any binary summation order, and finally divide by b_k, all in round-to-nearest arithmetic without underflow or overflow. Then the computed y_hat admits an exact componentwise backward representation in which c is unchanged, b_k*y_hat and each exact product a_i*b_i receive separate relative perturbations, and every perturbation has magnitude at most k*u. If b_k=1 and division is omitted, the bound improves to (k-1)*u. The unit-case proof constructs witnesses from one forward-error scalar epsilon by aligning signs with y_hat and each product; the analogous general construction is only implicit. There is no restriction on k and no O(u^2) remainder. [PDF p. 3 (printed 686), evaluation-order convention; PDF pp. 5-6 (printed 688-689), floating-point and inner-product model; PDF pp. 8-9 (printed 691-692), Corollary 3.2; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Lemma 4.1 and proof]
